reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes PLUS Token as a wallet and arbitrage service, invites viewers to delegate arbitrage, and claims monthly allocations of about 6% to 18% while saying entrusted assets are unaffected by price fluctuations. It also links sharing with friends to benefits from their entrusted bitcoin and presents additional percentage-based income across multiple layers. These are framed as product and income propositions rather than as a warning or investigation.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not treat the wallet as a risk-free account managed for users. It explicitly places control and responsibility with the private-key holder: only that person can control the assets, and the service offers no password access or transaction rollback. The speaker also says users can pause the automated feature. Those are meaningful operational limits alongside the income discussion, not a claim that the provider can recover funds or reverse mistakes.

The Plus Token does not provide access to the password, transaction rollback, and so on.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited monthly allocation describes purported arbitrage profits, but it does not establish that the speaker promises a fixed payment regardless of trading activity. The reference to price fluctuations concerns the entrusted digital assets; it is not a demonstration that any payout occurred. The private-key statement matters because it limits what the speaker says the platform itself controls.

citations.quote: the arbitrage profits about six percent to 18 percent of the monthly profit allocation to your wallet
The digital assets entrusted by users are completely unaffected by price fluctuations.
Only the user who controls the private key can control the assets of the corresponding account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Private-key responsibility and the ability to pause are not warnings that the advertised returns might fail. The speaker tells viewers they can delegate arbitrage, describes monthly profit allocations of about 6% to 18%, and says entrusted assets are completely unaffected by price fluctuations. Those affirmative assurances are central to the pitch, whatever limits are stated about password recovery.

opening.argument: Judge, this is structured as an explanation of how a digital wallet and its automated trading feature are supposed to work. The speaker announces a discussion of business applications and the revenue model, describes multi-currency storage and transaction settlement, then explains how the robot identifies price differences before deciding whether to trade. The percentage and referral examples can be read as illustrations of the described model; the cited material does not show a completed trade or an actual recipient of those example payments.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening correctly identifies an arbitrage explanation and layered calculations, but those quotations alone do not show realized returns. The speaker introduces the bitcoin calculation as an example. Explaining a revenue model, including its proposed referral formula, is distinguishable from evidence that the illustrated transactions actually took place.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is what the speaker promotes, not whether a trade or payout is independently verified. The explanation shifts into a direct invitation to delegate arbitrage, promises monthly profit allocations, and tells viewers they can receive commissions for sharing with friends. Calling the calculations examples does not turn that income pitch into a neutral demonstration.

opening.argument: Judge, the product described is a mobile wallet with storage, transaction settlement, exchange, and an optional automated arbitrage feature. The account-control description says the user retains the private key, while the trading explanation says the robot decides whether to undertake an arbitrage transaction. The referral figures are hypothetical calculations introduced with examples, not proof in this record that anyone transferred bitcoin, received a payout, or surrendered credentials. The narrower reading is a promotional explanation of a proposed service, without a demonstrated loss or completed transaction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening identifies proposed monthly returns and recruitment layers, but its quotations do not establish a completed deposit, a paid commission, or a request for a password. The transcript instead says only the private-key holder controls the account. The layered figures describe how the proposed referral program would calculate benefits; they are not records of benefits actually paid.

citations.quote: the arbitrage profits about six percent to 18 percent of the monthly profit allocation to your wallet
On the 2nd to 10th layers you can still take 10% of their smart gains
Only the user who controls the private key can control the assets of the corresponding account.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed loss or credential request is not necessary to assess the promotion. The speaker invites users to delegate arbitrage, claims monthly allocations from its profits, then offers a commission tied to friends' benefits and further income through multiple layers. Those features are expressly part of the offered service, not merely an ordinary wallet function; the private-key claim does not negate the promoted return and recruitment mechanism.
